matching.intro: To describe the process of Acceptance Matching we will use a real life example.
matching.life_example:
Assume that a Matchmaker invites 5 men and 5 women for a dinner and then asks each of them to spend sometime with each of the 5 candidates to decide whom are acceptable for future marriage.

Then the matchmaker asks each of the 10 guests to secretly write down his/her wishlist sorted by the most desired candidates.

The Matchmaker figures out that the best way to process those wishlists is by putting them in a table similar to the one below.
matching.results:
The Matchmaker studies this table and starts by marking mutual acceptances with red circles.
(8 mutually acceptanced couples were found).
There would be cases that one person would have more than one Mutual Acceptance.
To resolve these cases, Matchmaker assigns a score relative to the rank in the wishlists then give each Mutual Acceptance case the sum of the two scores of the two wishes of that couple.
Then choose the highest scores and come up with the final Matchlist.
matching.still_looking:
Some guests won't find successful matches.
Those always have free invitation for the following Matching dinner to try again.
matching.conclusion:
This is basically what KOBOOL does electronically every midnight (GMT).
As it processes hundreds of thousands of Acceptance Lists to connect whom have mutual acceptances for marriage.
